hints.content: $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to{-8}^+}g(x)$ represents the limit of $g$ as $x$ approaches $-8$ *from the right*.

Since we're only interested in how the function behaves as it approaches $x=-8$ from the right, we only need to look at this part of the table:

$x$ | $g(x)$
:-: | :-:
$-7.999$ | $0.008$
$-7.995$ | $0.04$
$-7.975$ | $0.2$

The $g(x)$-values seem to approach $0$.

question.content:
The function $g$ is defined over the real numbers. This table gives select values of $g$.

$x$ | $g(x)$
:-: | :-:
$-8.025$ | $-5.2$
$-8.005$ | $-5.04$
$-8.001$ | $-5.008$
$-8$ | $8$
$-7.999$ | $0.008$
$-7.995$ | $0.04$
$-7.975$ | $0.2$

**What is a reasonable estimate for $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to{-8}^+}g(x)$?**

[[☃ radio 1]]

choices.clue: This is the limit as $x$ approaches $-8$ from the left, not the right.
The value of the function at a particular $x$-value is not necessarily the same as the value of the limit. What $g$-value does the function appear to approach from the right?
The function appears to approach a specific function value from the right.
